newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo prosecutors indict four former DKB officials.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo prosecutors indict four former DKB officials.

text.p: Japanese public prosecutors indicted four former executives of Dai-ichi Kangyo Bank Ltd (DKB) on Thursday on charges of making loans of 11.78 billion yen to a corporate racketeer, prosecutors said.

In a statement, the Tokyo District Prosecutors' Office said the four DKB officials conspired to extend the loans in 51 installments to Ryuichi Koike through Tokyo-based financial institution Daiwa Shinyo from July 1994 to September 1996.
The indicted are former managing director Hiroshi Inotsume, former general affairs manager Tatsuo Shibuya, and former deputy general affairs managers Michiyoshi Kusajima and Takushi Manabe.
The four were the first DKB executives to be indicted in the current racketeer scandal which has also involved Japan's biggest brokerage, Nomura Securities Co Ltd.
The statement said the four DKB officials violated the Commercial Code which bans payoffs to racketeers.
Racketeers or "sokaiya" extort money by threatening to disrupt shareholders' meetings.
Prosecutors also said they indicted Koike for receiving the loans.

In a separate but related move, prosecutors said they re-arrested racketeer Koike and his younger brother Yoshinori Koike on suspicion of receiving 320 million yen in cash from Nomura Securities in March 1995.
Prosecutors said in a statement that the money was paid to the two for their pledge to ensure a smooth proceeding of Nomura's shareholders' meeting on June 29, 1995.
